questions.question: What are CSS custom properties (variables)? How do they enable theming?
questions.title: CSS Custom Properties & var() — Theming Made Easy
questions.direct_answer:
What are CSS custom properties (variables)? How do they enable theming?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** --name syntax, var(--name, fallback), inheritance, runtime JS access via getComputedStyle/setProperty, dark-mode theming.

**Classic weak answer:** Treating them like SCSS variables (compile-time) — CSS custom properties are runtime and can be changed by JS or :root selectors.

**Senior finish:** Show a dark-mode toggle with custom properties on :root[data-theme="dark"]; mention the @property API for typed custom props.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **CSS Custom Properties & var() — Theming Made Easy** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What are CSS custom properties (variables)? How do they enable theming?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **--name syntax, var(--name, fallback), inheritance, runtime JS access via getComputedStyle/setProperty, dark-mode theming**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Treating them like SCSS variables (compile-time) — CSS custom properties are runtime and can be changed by JS or :root selectors**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show a dark-mode toggle with custom properties on :root[data-theme="dark"]; mention the @property API for typed custom props**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** --name syntax, var(--name, fallback), inheritance, runtime JS access via getComputedStyle/setProperty, dark-mode theming
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **treating them like SCSS variables (compile-time) — CSS custom properties are runtime and can be changed by JS or :root selectors** and what you do instead.

- **Pitfall:** Treating them like SCSS variables (compile-time) — CSS custom properties are runtime and can be changed by JS or :root selectors

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **--name syntax, var(--name, fallback), inheritance, runtime JS access via getComputedStyle/setProperty, dark-mode theming** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Treating them like SCSS variables (compile-time) — CSS custom properties are runtime and can be changed by JS or :root selectors** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Show a dark-mode toggle with custom properties on :root[data-theme="dark"]; mention the @property API for typed custom props**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).
